entries.proposition: Table 2 lists the WWOX case as compound heterozygous for c.517-1G>A and an exon 5 deletion, both Pathogenic; the splice allele is marked ES-detectable and the deletion not. Nothing else in the main text concerns WWOX.
entries.snippet: Pt2317 WWOX c.517-1G>A Comp het P Yes Unclassified (Epilepsy) Ex5 DEL P No
entries.anchor: Table 2, row Pt2317 (JATS table, read cell-wise)

entries.proposition: The splice allele is an intron-5 canonical acceptor change (exon 6 acceptor) with no protein consequence given; its pathogenicity rests on rule-based and in-silico evidence (CADD 25.1; PVS1, PM2, PM3, PP3), not on an RNA assay.
The ACMG evidence for the splice allele is PVS1, PM2, PM3 and PP3, with CADD 25.1 and no SIFT/PolyPhen2 value.

entries.proposition: The second allele is a single-exon CNV, a deletion-insertion spanning WWOX exon 5, called by five SV callers; it is classified PVS1, PM2, PM3 with no RNA or protein measurement.
entries.snippet: B=1 exon CNV | C=Chr16:g.78140467_78313935delinsCA | D=WWOX exon 5 (NM_016373)

entries.proposition: The paper's RNA-seq was run on lymphoblastoid lines of selected non-WWOX cases (example: the CHASERR deletion case); no WWOX transcript was assayed.
entries.snippet: We therefore sought to determine the CHD2 expression level in Pt2190’s LCL in two independent RNA-seq batches.
